newsitem.title: USA: Intel comments brighten chip outlook.
newsitem.headline: Intel comments brighten chip outlook.

text.p: Intel Corp's surprise announcement late Monday that third quarter revenues are running better than expected should help pull the entire semiconductor group out of its malaise, analysts said.

Gruntal & Co analyst Mona Eraiba, who raised her 1996 and 1997 estimates on Intel following the announcement, said the news indicates market conditions for semiconductors in a key segment may finally be improving.
"Intel is saying the inventory adjustment in the PC market is over from a semiconductor point of view," Eraiba said. "So we expect all of the companies to start acting better."
Eraiba said she now expects Intel to earn $4.70 per share for 1996, up from her previous estimate of $4.55.
She also raised her 1997 estimate on the company to $5.80 per share from $5.30 and now rates Intel an outperform, up from long-term outperform.
Analysts said Intel's good news is almost certain to spark renewed interest in the sector, which has endured an extended period of eroded chip prices because of industry oversupply.
"There will will be significant spillover to the entire group," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "This could even filter down to the equipment suppliers."
Intel surged 5-3/8 to 94 within minutes of Tuesday's open and was Nasdaq's most active issue on volume of more than 4.8 million shares.
S3 Inc which supplies graphics accelerator chips for personal computers, rose 1-3/16 to 17-3/16 and integrated circuit maker Atmel Corp jumped 1-11/16 to 25-13/16.

Applied Materials Inc, which makes wafer fabrication systems for the semiconductor industry, gained 3/4 to 26-1/2. Applied Materials, S3 and Atmel were all among Nasdaq's 10 most active issues in early trading.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's Semiconductor Index .SOXX rose five points, or 2.9 percent, to 178.16. The Nasdaq Composite gained four points, or 0.34 percent, to 1198.
